_what: Q140(x): rank 4's paired-anchor rule, registered before any pool-7 claim (Q139's final critic, open rank 4; section 11 item 6). score_rank4.py beside this file applies it; RANK4-RULE.md says it in words.
rule: a card's scale is the median of its anchors' ratios to aifoundry3's; it must land within 1% of the pool's median ratio for floats, and within 2% for int8, in each session pair
pairing: E163 with E164 first; a later pool-7 session on either card pairs with the most recent pool-7 session on the other card before it. Each pair is scored from its own two sessions only. A family passes if it passes in every scored pair.
D: a tile's measured switching W over its format's zeros at 600 MHz: each session's registered primary reduction on Q139(u)'s footing (reduce_footing.K_FROZEN 0.2056 W/C on aifoundry3, 0.3134 W/C on card 1; E82 A2's dip rule once), the mean over the session's kept passes, as its power rules score it (E153's and E157's power_rows measured, pool_anchors measured_D)
anchor_ratio: r = D(card 1) / D(aifoundry3) per anchor, both from the same pair
card_scale: s_anchor = the median of the family's anchor ratios (floats: the mean of the middle two of four; int8: the mean of the two)
pool_median: s_pool = the median of D(card 1) / D(aifoundry3) over pool 7's non-anchor tiles of the family (any priority) measured in both sessions with D at or above pool_min_D_w on both cards: E157's X1 / X2 selection, on pool 7
verdict: PASS if |s_anchor / s_pool - 1| <= line_rel; FAIL if not; NOT SCORED (never PASS) if fewer than min_anchors anchors or fewer than 5 pool tiles of the family are measured on both cards

bootstrap.what: the pool median's 95% interval over tiles (reported, not a verdict)

reported_not_verdicts: each anchor's ratio, and its standard error from the passes (each card's sd over its passes / sqrt(n), in quadrature on the ratio) where per-pass values exist
the mean of the anchor ratios beside their median
the E78 arm: s_anchor with E78's fp32.randn and fp16.randn (floats) and int8.full (int8) joined, if both sessions ran them
per format (fp32, fp16): the format's two anchors' median against the format's own pool median
s_anchor and s_pool against the card-1 terms the frozen models apply (M9 and M8 0.9616 for every format; M7 and M6 0.9711 floats, 0.9735 int8)
the per-tile transfer: the relative rms of the pool tiles' ratios about s_anchor and about s_pool

forecast.basis: pool 6, post hoc (Q139's final critic, re-derived by Q140(c)'s check 3 in docs/reports/data/2026-11-04-q140c-critic-checks/check3-anchor-card-scale.json): E78's and pool 6's random anchors on E153 and E157 gave floats 0.9618 against the pool's 0.9632 (-0.15%) and int8 0.9580 against 0.9681 (-1.04%, +-1.5% from the anchors' passes)
forecast.floats: PASS: about -0.15%, against a line of 1%; the difference's standard error is about 0.16% (the four anchors' 0.10% from their passes and the pool median's 0.12%, its 95% interval [0.9613, 0.9659] over 25 tiles), so a miss would take a real offset of about 1%
forecast.int8: PASS more likely than not, not secure: about -1%; card 1's int8 anchor read 3.6% sd over its three passes in E157, so the two anchors' scale carries a standard error of 1.2-1.5% (1.2% from both anchors' own passes, score_rank4.py's self-test; 1.5% in check 3, which took E78's tile's spread for pool 6's anchor) and the pool median 0.66% (95% interval [0.9534, 0.9783] over 16 tiles); the difference's is 1.35-1.64%, so the chance of landing inside +-2% is 69-75% with pool 6's -1.04% offset and 78-86% with none (normal approximation). More card-1 passes narrow it
